content.summary_of_the_paper: Currently, the evaluation of physical adversarial attacks is usually conducted by asking a few volunteers to attach the adversarial patches. It is very challenging to ensure the reproducibility of most attack algorithms under complex physical conditions. This paper proposed to simulate the complex transformations of faces in the physical world via 3D-face modelling and conduct reproducible evaluations conveniently to evaluate the performance of physical attacks on face recognition.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

The convenient evaluation mechanism can help researchers improve their physical attacks in a controllable virtual environment, which made a non-trivial contribution to the field of adversarial attacks on face recognition. Besides, 3D adversarial patches crafted by Face3DAdv generated robust adversarial patches in adversarial scenarios based on the simulator. The experimental results also illustrated the effectiveness against black-box recognition systems and commercial defensive mechanisms.


Weakness:

1. In Figure 4, I found that this method obtained a better black-box performance even in the axis of face conditions belonging to zero, and what caused this phenomenon of better performance? It would be very interesting if the author could add more discussion on this aspect.

2. In Table 1, I also noticed that the performance of Face3DAdv(w) is obviously better than Face3DAdv(x), which means that optimizing the latent space of a generative model is a better choice than directly optimizing face images. Is there any intuitive explanation?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The writing of this paper is clear. This paper proposed to simulate the complex transformations of faces in the physical world via 3D-face modelling and the idea is novel. The double blink online code also ensure the reproducibility of the proposed method.

There needs some clarification and explanation in the revision.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposes a novel framework for systematically and fairly evaluating attacks on face
recognition algorithms in the physical world. The framework simulates faces in the physical
world using 3D face modeling and implementing various transformations on the digitally
simulated faces. The authors propose an attack called Face3DAdv that generates adversarial
images based on 3d face transformations and physical variations. They further use a
probability-based importance score to carefully pick transformations to be used for creating
adversarial images.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Contribution
The work makes the following contributions: 
1. A systematic and fair 3D modeling-based framework for evaluating various attacks on face recognition algorithms under complex transformations like different viewpoints and lightning.
2. An attack algorithm that optimizes texture map (or latent code in second variation of attack) under carefully sampled transformations based on an importance probability score.

Pros
● The paper argues the need for systematic review of physical attacks for fair comparison. They also make case for complex transformations required to craft robust adversarial images. The authors have shown extensive experiments for the proposed attack by
varying pitch, Yaw, Lightning and a Mixture of three with different face recognition models in both white-box and black-box settings.
● The authors have proposed detailed testing protocol with extensive experiments and baselining.

Cons
● Though the authors mention that 3D printing is expensive, the authors have shown the success rate of their attack in the physical world with only 10 volunteers. 
● The proposed Face3DAdv method seems like plug and play and lacks algorithmic novelty.
● No experiment is used to justify the claim that the proposed algorithm is reproducible. Another set of experiments can be used to show the example images generated at different time instances for the same sample using different algorithms and how such
images affect the face recognition accuracy. (to confirm the reproducibility)
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
All the mathematical formulations and algorithmic notations seem correct.

However, another set of experiments can be used to show the example images generated at different time instances for the same sample using different algorithms and how such images affect the face recognition accuracy - to confirm the reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: I have been working in the focus areas of the paper and am up to date with the recent literature.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
